Japanese eggs are produced to be eaten raw — crack it straight into the mixed noodles and it coats everything. The soft-boiled one is usually soy-marinated, so ask if gluten matters.

items.ja: トッピング メンマ／キムチ
items.note: メンマ (menma) is bamboo shoot fermented then simmered in seasoning — the crunchy pale sticks in almost every ramen bowl, usually simmered in soy and often dashi. キムチ is Korean fermented cabbage, commonly containing fish sauce or salted shrimp. Both ¥100.

items.ja: トッピング チャーシュー
items.note: More slices on top.

items.ja: コーラ or オレンジ
items.note: One button, your pick of the two.
Barley beer. The aemen panel also carries チューハイ ¥400 and ハイボール ¥450, though both were showing sold-out lamps when photographed.

kyr_yume_wa_chikara_nari.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Read off a photograph of the shop's ticket machine dated 2026-06, plus its counter cards dated 2026-05 and 2026-07. The shop rebuilt the machine some time after October 2025: it used to be organised by noodle weight and pork-slice count (200g/300g × 豚1枚/豚2枚) and is now organised by FLAVOUR at a flat 200g. Older listings showing the 豚1枚/豚2枚 grid are obsolete. ¥1,000 for a 200g bowl is confirmed by a dated June 2026 first-hand visit.

items.note: The default bowl and the one most people order. 二郎系 (Jiro-style) means a soy-and-pork-fat broth under a mountain of boiled beansprouts and cabbage, with 豚 (buta) — not delicate chashu but thick fatty slabs of braised pork. Every bowl is 200g of 全粒粉超極太麺, wholemeal ultra-thick noodles, which the shop makes itself. Their own chart: a standard ramen is about 150g, so 200g is roughly 1.5 servings.

汁なし (shirunashi) = 'no soup'. Same mountain of vegetables and pork, but the tare and fat sit at the bottom of the bowl instead of a broth — mix hard from underneath before the first bite. Regulars add a raw egg to dip into.

塩 (shio) = salt rather than soy as the seasoning base. Cleaner and lighter-tasting than the shoyu, though still a heavy pork bowl. Shio tare often still contains some soy or wheat-derived seasoning, so it is not a gluten-free route without asking.
The salt version without soup.
担担 (tantan) is the Sichuan-derived sesame-paste and chilli style, here built on the Jiro frame. Nutty, numbing and rich.
汁なし担担麺 is a dish in its own right across Japan — thick sesame-chilli paste at the bottom, mixed up through the noodles.
辛味噌 = spicy miso. Miso can be barley-based (麦味噌), a second wheat-family risk on top of the soy.
梅 (ume) is the salted, intensely sour Japanese pickled plum. An unusual thing to meet in a Jiro bowl — the sharp acidity cuts straight through the fat, which is exactly the point.
The ume version without soup.

items.ja: やさい・あぶら・にんにく（コール）
items.en: The counter call — the three free choices
items.note: This is the moment travellers panic. As your bowl is handed over, staff ask three things IN THIS ORDER: ① やさい (yasai, the beansprout-and-cabbage mountain) ② あぶら (abura, melted pork back-fat spooned on top) ③ にんにく (ninniku, raw crushed garlic). For each, answer with one word — なし (nashi, none) / 少なめ (sukuname, less) / 普通 (futsuu, normal). All three of those are FREE. If you want more than normal, マシ (mashi) and マシマシ (mashi-mashi) must be bought as tickets at the machine first — you cannot call for them at the counter.

items.ja: 野菜マシマシのルール
items.en: House rules on ordering the biggest vegetable pile
items.note: A hand-written board next to the machine sets three conditions: 初来店の方はひかえて下さい — first-time visitors should NOT order マシマシ; 購入後の返金はしません — no refunds once bought; 食べ残しは追加料金いただきます — leaving food unfinished incurs an extra charge. Read as friendly but meant seriously. On a first visit, answer 普通.
豚 (buta) here means the thick fatty braised pork block, not thin chashu. This button upgrades you to a bigger piece.

Takes the bowl from 200g to 300g. Going the other way is free but must be done in person: the machine's sign says 麺の量を減らされるお客様は食券を買わないでお席で直接ご注文ください — if you want LESS noodle, do not buy a ticket, order at your seat.

items.en: Extra vegetables — one step or two
items.note: The button carries two levels: 1枚マシ (one step up) and 2枚マシマシ (two steps). Boiled beansprouts and cabbage, piled well above the rim at the top level.

items.en: Extra pork back-fat — one step or two
items.note: Same two levels, 1枚マシ and 2枚マシマシ. Melted back-fat spooned over the top, which is what makes a Jiro bowl heavy.
A Jiro-style habit that sounds wrong and works — it melts into the fat and tare.
Served in a small dish. On the brothless bowls, dip the noodles into it sukiyaki-style; on the soup bowls, crack it in.

Bottom-right button on the machine. The label says 内容、金額はSNSで告知 — what it is and what it costs are announced only on the shop's social media, so check that before you go. The shop also runs frequent handwritten 限定 (gentei, limited) boards by the door: recent ones have included a summer ユメメカ風ピビン麺, a cold lemon-and-corn tantan, and a 500g noodle challenge.

items.ja: 豚なし ご希望のお客様
items.en: Skip the pork, take ¥200 of toppings instead
items.note: A yellow counter card: if you do not want the pork slab, you may pick ¥200 worth from the list below free — just say so when you put your ticket down (食券を置かれた際にお声かけ下さい). Note this does NOT make the bowl vegetarian; the broth and tare are still pork-based.

items.ja: 味変しょうが／カレー／マヨネーズ／ゆずこしょう
items.note: 味変 (aji-hen) means 'flavour change' — something stirred in halfway through so the second half tastes different. Ginger cuts the fat; curry and mayonnaise enrich it; 柚子胡椒 is fermented green chilli with yuzu peel and salt, and despite the name contains no black pepper. Japanese curry roux contains wheat flour; mayonnaise is egg-based.
Sliced green onion, fresh against all that fat.
ちょい (choi) means 'just a bit'. Fried rice is wok-fried with soy sauce, so unlike plain rice it is not gluten-free.
黒ウーロン茶 is a more heavily oxidised oolong sold in Japan as a cut-through-grease drink, which is why a Jiro shop stocks it.

items.ja: 卓上調味料（カエシ・酢・一味・ブラックペッパー）
items.note: Four bottles, all free. カエシ (kaeshi) is the concentrated soy tare — the card says use it 味が薄い時に, when the bowl tastes flat; it is wheat soy. 酢 (su) vinegar cuts the fat. 一味 (ichimi) is pure ground red chilli. Plus black pepper. When you finish, put the bowl, cup and chopsticks up on the counter and bin your tissues in the black bin behind you.

kyr_menya_roman.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Taken from the shop's own official site and the shop-managed menu page it links to, cross-checked against photographs of the shop's own bilingual street A-boards dated 2026-01, the month it opened.

items.note: The house bowl. 鶏白湯 (tori-paitan) is chicken bones boiled hard for hours until the broth emulsifies into something opaque and almost soupy-thick. The shop uses さつま知覧どり, Kagoshima hens raised 450 days — older birds, deeper flavour — simmered with vegetables into what they call their 黄金スープ, golden soup. Give it a stir before the first spoonful; it separates.

items.ja: 極上 鶏チャーシュー麺
items.en: Deluxe ramen loaded with chicken chashu
items.note: 極上 (gokujo) = 'finest'. Flagged by the shop as 人気NO.1, their best seller: the paitan bowl covered in slices of low-cooked chicken chashu rather than pork.

items.ja: 京都九条ネギラーメン
items.en: Ramen heaped with Kyoto Kujo green onion
items.note: 九条ねぎ (Kujo negi) is Kyoto's own green onion, named for the Kujo district and grown here for over a thousand years — thicker, sweeter and softer than ordinary scallion, with a slippery gel inside the leaf. Piled on in a green mound over the chicken broth. The most local order on this menu.

items.ja: 和牛ラーメン【黒毛和牛 A5ランク】
items.en: Ramen topped with A5 wagyu beef
items.note: 黒毛和牛 is Japanese Black, the main wagyu breed; A5 is the top grade for marbling. Slices are laid over the hot broth so they cook only just through. Nearly three times the price of the standard bowl — an occasion dish, not a normal ramen order.

items.ja: 鶏チャーシューもやし
items.note: 逸品 (ippin) heads this section — 'choice items', the small plates. Sliced chicken chashu over dressed beansprouts.
Fried chicken tossed in 양념 (yangnyeom) sauce — sweet, garlicky, moderately spicy, sticky. Gochujang chilli paste normally contains wheat, and the chicken is battered.

items.ja: とり南蛮 しば漬けタルタル
items.en: Sweet-vinegar fried chicken with Kyoto-pickle tartare
items.note: チキン南蛮 is fried chicken dipped in sweet vinegar sauce and topped with tartare — a Miyazaki dish. The Kyoto twist here is しば漬け (shibazuke), the purple-red pickle of eggplant and cucumber cured with red shiso, chopped into the tartare. Battered and soy-seasoned.
とろとろ means so soft it collapses. 豚足 (tonsoku) is pig's foot, slow-braised until the collagen goes to jelly — an izakaya classic, mostly skin and gelatin rather than meat.
The cheapest thing on the menu, and a good palate-cutter against the thick broth. Kimchi seasoning commonly contains fish sauce or salted shrimp.
Marinated in soy and ginger, starch-coated, deep-fried. The default beer companion in Japan.
せんべい normally means a rice cracker; here it describes the texture — chicken skin pressed and fried until it shatters like one. Salty, very crisp.

items.ja: 和牛ユッケ重【A5黒毛和牛】
items.note: ユッケ (yukke) is the Korean-Japanese raw seasoned beef, usually with a raw egg yolk on top; 重 (ju) means it is served in a lacquered box over rice. Raw beef — worth knowing before you order. Seasoned with soy.
The shop's chicken chashu over rice with an egg yolk — the standard side to a ramen here.

items.en: How to order — by QR code on your phone
items.note: There is no ticket machine to puzzle over and no Japanese-only menu to read: the shop posts bilingual instructions. ① Scan the QR code at the counter and pick your items and toppings from the phone menu. ② Sign in to confirm the order — Apple ID, Google account and LINE all work. ③ Pay on the phone. ④ Hold the resulting QR code up to the ticket printer, take the printed 食券 (meal ticket) and hand it to staff. Only 8 seats, so expect to wait at busy times.

items.ja: 鶏白湯らーめん 塩「塩のキラメキ®」
items.romaji: tori-paitan raamen shio / Shio no Kirameki
items.note: Paitan (白湯) means the chicken bones were boiled hard enough to emulsify — thick, opaque, almost soup-like-gravy, not the clear broth most people expect. Kirameki mill their own noodles (自家製麺). Sizes on the board: 小 (ko, small) ¥800 / 並 (nami, regular) ¥850 / 大 (dai, large) ¥930 / 特大 (tokudai, extra large) ¥1,010 — point at the size word, they cost different amounts.

items.ja: 鶏白湯らーめん 醤油「醤油のキラメキ®」
items.romaji: tori-paitan raamen shouyu / Shouyu no Kirameki
items.note: Same thick chicken broth as the shio, but the seasoning base (タレ, tare) is soy sauce, so it is darker and rounder. Same size ladder: 小¥800 / 並¥850 / 大¥930 / 特大¥1,010.

items.ja: 極濃鶏白湯まぜそば GTM
items.en: Brothless noodles in ultra-thick chicken paitan sauce
items.note: GTM is the shop's own abbreviation. まぜそば (mazesoba) = 'mixed noodles': there is no soup, just a very reduced chicken sauce sitting at the bottom with the toppings. Stir it hard from the bottom before the first bite or the top half is dry. 小¥920 / 並¥970 / 大¥1,070 / 特¥1,170.

items.en: The GTM mazesoba loaded with everything
items.note: DX = デラックス, deluxe — the same bowl with extra chashu pork, a marinated egg, kimchi and sheets of nori piled on. 小¥1,220 / 並¥1,270 / 大¥1,370 / 特¥1,470.

items.ja: 麻辣シビカラ台湾まぜそば
items.note: 麻辣 (málà) is the Sichuan pairing of chilli heat (辣) with the tingling numbness of Sichuan pepper (麻); シビカラ is the Japanese slang for the same thing — shibireru (numb) + karai (hot). The flyer warns シビレル辛さがクセになる — 'the numbing heat is addictive'. Spicy by design; no mild version. 小/並¥950, 大/特¥1,050.

items.ja: 台湾まぜそば 直太朗
items.en: The plain Taiwan mazesoba — brothless noodles with spicy minced pork and raw egg yolk
items.note: Despite the name, 台湾まぜそば is a Nagoya invention. No soup: chilli-hot minced pork (台湾ミンチ), chives, garlic, nori and a raw yolk sit on thick noodles over a pool of tare. Break the yolk, stir everything hard, then eat. When about a third is left, ask for 追い飯 (oimeshi) — a scoop of rice tipped into the leftover sauce — if the shop offers it that day. 小/並/大¥900, 特¥1,000, メガ (mega) ¥1,000.

items.en: Taiwan mazesoba with the full topping load
items.note: Same bowl as the 直太朗 plus chashu, two egg halves, kimchi and extra nori. 小/並¥1,160, 大/特¥1,260.

items.ja: 台湾まぜそば 豚キムチーズ
items.en: Taiwan mazesoba with pork, kimchi and melting cheese
items.note: 豚 (buta, pork) + キムチ (kimchi) + チーズ (cheese), squashed into one word. Shredded cheese melts into the hot noodles and takes the edge off the chilli. 小/並¥1,060, 大/特¥1,160.

items.en: House topping set: +2 slices pork, +1 marinated egg, +3 sheets of nori
items.note: The flyer spells out exactly what you get: 肉+2枚・煮玉子+1個・海苔+3枚. Comes in a 塩 version and a まぜそば version — say which bowl you ordered. Note that on the Kirameki Special the chashu already in the bowl is increased rather than added on top.
増量 (zouryou) is the word to look for on any Japanese menu — it means 'increased quantity' of whatever precedes it.
Shredded cheese for melting into a mazesoba. Only served on the wheat noodles, so it is not a gluten-free option in practice.
Also written 味玉 (ajitama) elsewhere — the same thing: a jammy-yolked egg steeped in a soy-and-mirin marinade. The marinade is soy sauce, which in Japan is wheat-brewed by default.
The chilli-and-garlic minced pork that defines a Taiwan mazesoba — order more of it if you want the bowl hotter.
ネギ (negi) is the green onion piled on almost every bowl. Cheap way to cut the richness of a paitan broth.
枚 (mai) is the counter for flat things — 3枚 is three sheets. Nori itself is just seaweed, but it goes into a wheat-noodle bowl here.

items.en: Japanese fried chicken + rice, added to any noodle order
items.note: The big red flash on the flyer reads お好きな麺類＋270円 — 'any noodle dish you like, plus ¥270' — and 終日お得 means the deal runs all day, not just at lunch. Kara-age is marinated in soy and dusted in wheat/potato starch before frying.

items.en: Rice bowl topped with the shop's pork and spring onion
items.note: 丼 (don/donburi) = a bowl of rice with something on top. Add-on price when ordered with any noodle dish.
Add-on price with any noodle dish. Kimchi in Japan is usually seasoned with fish sauce or dried shrimp as well as soy.

items.en: Plain white rice, regular or large
items.note: Plain unseasoned steamed rice — genuinely safe on both counts as long as nothing is poured over it. 並 = regular, 大 = large; the flyer prices both at ¥170.

items.en: Fried chicken, sold by the piece
items.note: 個 (ko) is the counter for small round things — 1個 is one piece, so you can order exactly as many as you want. Soy marinade plus a flour/starch coating.

kyr_men_to_sake_no_tora.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Core menu prices read from photographs of the shop's own printed menu card and paper order sheet dated July 2026; the 酒と寅のアテ side-dish list is from an October 2025 photograph of the same menu folder.

items.note: 汁あり literally means 'with liquid'. Supervised by Kyoto tantanmen house 金鶏楼 and marked 人気NO.1！まずはこれ！ — 'most popular, start here'. You do not order verbally: staff hand you an オーダーシート (order sheet) and you circle your choices. On it you set 麺のかたさ (noodle firmness: かため firm / 基本 standard / やわめ soft), ねぎ (spring onion: なし none / あり yes), 肉味噌 (minced-pork miso: なし / あり), then two 0–5 dials — 辣油 (rāyu, chilli oil; 2 is 基本, the default) and 花椒 (huājiāo, Sichuan pepper, the numbing one; 1 is default). Circle 基本 everywhere if you are unsure — the sheet itself says the standard settings are recommended for first-timers. A half portion, 汁ありハーフサイズ, is ¥800.

汁なし = 'no liquid'. Sesame paste, chilli oil and minced pork sit in the bottom of the bowl with no broth at all — stir hard from the bottom before the first bite or you eat plain noodles then a puddle of sauce. Two extra options unlock on the order sheet for this version only: 葱油 (negi-abura, spring-onion oil) and フライドオニオン (crisp fried onion), each なし/あり. The menu note お酒にもごはんにも合います means it goes with both the sake and a bowl of rice — ordering a 白ごはん to mop the bowl out is the intended finish.
夏季限定 = summer only (in 2026 from 14 May), 一日限定10食 = ten bowls a day, then it is gone. Served with a mortar so you grind the sesame yourself and a citrus wedge to squeeze over — 胡麻をお好みにすり、柑橘をギュッと絞って.

The menu states 動物由来原料不使用 — 'no animal-derived ingredients' — and describes the base as お昆布とお豆さんのチカラ, 'the power of kombu and beans', i.e. kelp stock and soy instead of the usual pork-and-chicken. That is the shop's own written claim and it is unusually explicit for Japan, where hidden bonito dashi is the norm; still worth confirming the chilli oil is the plain one. Wheat noodles, so not gluten-free. Spice level adjustable like the others.

items.en: Kids' dan dan noodles (not spicy) with a toy
items.note: からくない汁あり担担麺＋おもちゃ — the soup version with the heat taken out, plus a toy. Also the fallback if you cannot handle chilli at all.

items.en: Slow-cooked soft egg, added on top
items.note: 温泉玉子 (onsen tamago), short form 温玉 — cooked slowly at low temperature so the white is barely set and the yolk is custardy. Break it into a soupless bowl and it turns the sauce creamy.
追い (oi-) as a prefix means 'chase it with more' — you will meet it again as 追い飯 (extra rice) and 追いしば漬け below. Written ねぎ増し on the wall menu.
大盛 (oomori) is the standard Japanese word for an upsized portion — you will see it on every noodle menu in the country. Here it is spelled out as 1.5倍, one and a half times.
しば漬け is one of Kyoto's three classic pickles: aubergine and cucumber salted with red shiso leaf, magenta and sharply sour. A local touch on a Sichuan dish — the acidity cuts the sesame fat.
肉味噌 is pork mince fried down with miso and aromatics — the savoury heart of a tantanmen. The order sheet notes it is made with 花椒 (Sichuan pepper).

items.en: The gritty sediment from the chilli oil, for extra heat
items.note: 滓 (kasu) is the solid dregs left at the bottom of the chilli-oil jar — chilli flakes and aromatics, far hotter than the oil itself. 辛増 = more heat. Fifty yen, and the cheapest way to make the bowl serious.

items.en: Add 2 pieces of fried chicken + a small rice to any tantanmen
items.note: The set price is the ADD-ON, not the total: お好きな担担麺＋鶏の唐揚げ2個＋ごはん小 — 'the tantanmen of your choice, plus two pieces of kara-age, plus a small rice'.

items.en: Add 2 fried chicken wings + a small rice
items.note: 手羽 (teba) is the chicken wing; 手羽から is the shop's contraction of 手羽唐揚げ, fried wings. 寅 (Tora, 'tiger') is the shop's own name attached to its signature version.

items.en: Add 2 boiled dumplings + a small rice
items.note: 水餃子 = boiled (not pan-fried) dumplings, thicker and slippery-skinned. Wheat wrappers, soy in the filling.

items.en: Rice topped with minced-pork miso and a soft egg
items.note: The house rice bowl. Three sizes: 小 (small) ¥500 / 中 (chū, medium) ¥550 / 大 (large) ¥600 — 小・中・大 is the size ladder you will see everywhere in Japan.

items.ja: 白ごはん（八代目儀兵衛）
items.en: Plain white rice, from Kyoto rice merchant Hachidaime Gihei
items.note: 白ごはん = plain steamed white rice, nothing added — genuinely gluten-free and vegan. 八代目儀兵衛 is a well-known Kyoto rice shop, so this is better rice than the usual side. 小¥200 / 中¥250 / 大¥300. Order one to finish a 汁なし bowl with.

たたき (tataki) means the outside is flashed over high heat and the inside left raw, then sliced and served cold with a ponzu-type sauce. アテ (ate) is Kansai slang for a small dish eaten with drink — the Tokyo word is おつまみ. Ponzu contains soy sauce.
Chicken marinated in soy, sake and ginger, dusted in starch and flour, fried twice. 個 (ko) counts the pieces.

items.en: The house fried chicken wings, 3 pieces
items.note: Wings rather than thigh meat — more skin, more to gnaw, better with beer.
Same starch-and-flour treatment as fried chicken, applied to octopus — chewy inside, crisp outside.

items.en: Spring rolls with whatever is in season
items.note: 季節の (kisetsu no) = 'of the season' — the filling changes through the year, so ask what is in them today. Wheat wrapper.
水 (mizu/sui) = water — boiled, not fried. Slippery thick skins, eaten with a vinegar-and-soy dip.
焼き (yaki) = grilled/fried — the familiar crisp-bottomed gyoza. Wheat wrapper, soy in the filling and the dip.

items.en: Cold tofu, the shop's 'most fearsome' version
items.note: 冷奴 (hiyayakko) is chilled block tofu, normally a mild dish with ginger and soy. 最恐 is a pun — 最強 means 'strongest', but written with 恐 (fear) it means 'scariest', i.e. this one is loaded with chilli. Toppings usually include soy sauce and often bonito flakes, so confirm before treating it as vegan.
杏仁豆腐 is not tofu at all — it is a set milk pudding flavoured with apricot kernel, the standard Chinese-restaurant dessert. やわらか = soft-set. Usually made with dairy and sometimes gelatine.

kyr_kirin_en_2.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The shop's own English menu marks most a-la-carte prices as pre-tax (税抜); the lunch sets and the whole 激辛 sheet are marked tax-included.

items.en: Extra-hot dan dan noodles — the shop's trophy dish
items.section: 激辛メニュー / Super-spicy menu
items.note: Won the gold prize at the first KARA-1 Grand Prix, Japan's national hot-food contest. Chicken-bone broth thickened with sesame paste, four kinds of chilli plus golden chilli, finished with ghost pepper (ジョロキア); house meat-miso over special curly noodles. You pick the heat 1-5 — levels 3/4/5 cost +¥150/+¥300/+¥450, and level 1 is already properly hot.

items.section: 激辛メニュー / Super-spicy menu
items.note: Summer only (夏季限定). Cold noodles with roast pork and colourful vegetables; same 1-5 heat scale, and you can order it at normal strength.

items.section: 激辛メニュー / Super-spicy menu
items.note: Muko City runs a 激辛商店街 — a 'super-spicy shopping street' of about 70 shops started in 2009 — and this restaurant is a member; the whole spicy sheet exists because of it.

items.section: 激辛メニュー / Super-spicy menu
items.note: The cheapest way into the spicy menu; tofu and minced pork in chilli-bean sauce ladled over a bowl of rice.
The house's plain bowl — the English menu calls the broth 'chicken glass soup', meaning a clear rather than cloudy stock. This is the bowl the ¥1,000 A Lunch set is built around.
Same bowl as the plain ramen, blanketed with slices of the house roast pork (自家製やきぶた, which is also sold as an appetiser).

items.en: 'Five-things' ramen — ramen under a mixed stir-fry
items.note: 五目 literally means 'five items' but really just signals a generous mix — pork, squid, prawn and vegetables stir-fried and tipped over the noodles. A version with egg is ¥1,000.
Broth seasoned with fermented soybean paste. Miso is frequently barley-based (mugi-miso), so it is doubly out for gluten avoiders.
The non-lethal version of the award-winning bowl: sesame-and-chilli broth with minced pork. The menu notes the spice is adjustable from mild up to level 5.

items.ja: 酸辣麺（四川式辛味あんかけ）
items.note: The noodle version of hot-and-sour soup — vinegar sharpness against chilli heat, in a starch-thickened あんかけ (ankake) sauce poured over the noodles.

items.ja: 焼きそば（広東風あんかけ）
items.note: Not the sweet-sauce street-festival yakisoba: noodles crisped in the pan, then drowned in a savoury starch-thickened seafood-and-vegetable gravy.

items.ja: 皿うどん（広東風あんかけ）
items.en: 'Plate udon' — crisp fried noodles under gravy
items.note: A Nagasaki Chinese-Japanese dish despite the name — no udon involved. Fine noodles fried to a shattering crisp, softening under the gravy as you eat.

items.ja: 揚げそば（広東風あんかけ）
items.en: Deep-fried noodle nest with Cantonese gravy
items.note: Called かた焼きそば (kata-yakisoba) elsewhere — the crunchy-noodle cousin of the pan-fried version.

items.ja: 冷 麺（5月～8月の季節限定）
items.note: May to August only. In a Japanese Chinese restaurant 冷麺 means cold noodles fanned with ham, egg, cucumber and tomato in a sweet-sour dressing — not the Korean buckwheat naengmyeon. A chilled dan dan version is also ¥1,000.

items.ja: フカヒレラーメン（姿煮入り）
items.en: Ramen with a whole braised shark's fin
items.note: The banquet flourish of the noodle page — an entire braised fin laid on the bowl. The kitchen also serves the fin alone at ¥12,000, and asks for about 30 minutes.
Kansai says やきめし where Tokyo says 炒飯 (chahan) — the same dish. Comes with soup. Seasoned with wheat soy sauce, and it contains egg and pork.
The house's signature fried rice — lettuce folded in at the last second so it stays crunchy. It is also the rice course inside the ¥2,850 KIRIN Lunch.

items.en: Crab omelette over rice in thick sauce
items.note: Invented in Japan, not in Tianjin: a fluffy crab-and-egg omelette draped over rice and flooded with glossy starch-thickened sauce. A machi-chuka staple.

items.en: Rice bowl under a mixed stir-fry
items.note: The 八宝菜 stir-fry — pork, squid, prawn, cabbage, carrot — poured straight over rice. Comes with soup.
Small ¥250 / regular ¥350 / large ¥450. Unseasoned white rice — the one genuinely gluten-free, vegan thing on the page.

items.section: 餃子・点心 / Dumplings & dim sum
items.note: The menu's own advice is to eat them with a slice of raw onion. Wheat wrappers, and the dip is soy-based.

items.section: 餃子・点心 / Dumplings & dim sum
items.note: Same filling as the fried ones but poached, so the wheat skin stays slippery and thick rather than crisp.

items.section: 餃子・点心 / Dumplings & dim sum
items.note: Shanghai-style — jellied stock melts into broth inside the wrapper as they steam. Bite a small hole and sip first, or you get scalded.

items.section: 餃子・点心 / Dumplings & dim sum
items.note: Glutinous-rice dough rolled in sesame and fried, sweet bean paste inside. Rice-based, but shares a fryer with wheat-battered food. Strawberry and matcha versions are ¥700.

items.section: スープ・デザート / Soup & dessert
items.note: The default Chinese-restaurant dessert in Japan — apricot-kernel-flavoured milk jelly, wobbly and barely sweet. Contains dairy.

kyr_aji_no_tentoku_kyoto_shi.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Read from a January 2026 photograph of this branch's own ticket machine; the operator's corporate site publishes no prices for any branch, so nothing here is imported from another shop.

items.note: The whole reason the shop exists. 油そば = 'oil noodles': NO SOUP. A secret soy tare and blended vegetable oils sit hidden under the noodles; chashu, menma, spring onion, nori and half an egg go on top. THE RITUAL: stir hard from the bottom first, then reach for the two big bottles on the counter — お酢 (osu, vinegar) and ラー油 (rāyu, chilli oil) — and add a circuit of each, then stir again. The shop's own instruction card says the vinegar is the key (ポイントはお酢). There is grated garlic (おろしにんにく) in a pot on the counter too. Buy a ticket at the 券売機 (ticket machine) BEFORE sitting; the machine takes only OLD-style banknotes and will not accept the new ¥500 coin — hand new notes to the owner to swap. Machine price ¥850 = ¥773 + ¥77 tax.
Same bowl, salt-based tare instead of soy — lighter and cleaner, and reviewers describe it as the richer-tasting of the two despite that. Same vinegar-and-chilli-oil ritual.

items.ja: 油そば　醤油味　大盛
items.note: 大盛 (oomori) = large. The shop has historically sold this as ダブル/320g — double noodles for the same amount of tare, so it eats drier; add a little more vinegar. Its size names are worth knowing if you see them written out: ひかえめ/ハーフ 80g, ていばん/シングル 160g, まんぷく/ダブル 320g, はらきれ/トリプル 480g — literally 'modest', 'standard', 'full belly', 'burst stomach'.

items.ja: 油そば　塩味　大盛
items.note: Double noodles, salt tare. Machine price ¥1,100 = ¥1,000 + ¥100 tax.

items.ja: 油そば　シンプル　塩味
items.en: Stripped-back abura-soba — noodles and tare, minimal toppings
items.note: シンプル (simple) is the bare version without the full topping load. Regulars order it as a 〆 (shime) — the noodle dish that closes a night of drinking, which is exactly what this shop is for: it opens at 18:00 and runs to 23:00.

items.ja: ライスセット　醤油
items.en: Soy abura-soba with a bowl of rice
items.note: The English on the button reads 'Original sauce noodles, soy sauce taste, with rice'. The rice is there to be tipped into the bowl at the end to mop up the leftover tare — the same idea as 追い飯 (oimeshi) at a mazesoba shop.

items.en: Salt abura-soba with a bowl of rice
items.note: Same set, salt tare.

Machine price ¥380 = ¥345 + ¥35 tax. The counter has a 餃子たれ (gyoza dip) bottle alongside the vinegar and chilli oil. Wheat wrappers and soy in both filling and dip. The top row of the machine also carries two ¥1,200 buttons whose pictures pair a plate of these gyoza with a bowl of abura-soba — that is the noodles-plus-gyoza set, if you want both. Their kanji labels were too blurred in the photograph to transcribe, so they are not listed here as separate items.

玉 (tama) is the counter for a portion-ball of noodles — 1玉 is one serving's worth. The button's English reads 'One noodles addition'. Different from 替玉 (kaedama, a refill served later at a tonkotsu shop): here you buy it up front and it comes in the same bowl.
Labelled in English on the machine as 'Boiled egg, soy sauce taste' — which tells you plainly that it has been steeped in wheat-brewed soy.

items.ja: トッピング　キムチ
items.note: Its acidity works like the vinegar, cutting the oil. Japanese kimchi usually contains fish sauce or dried shrimp as well as soy.

items.en: The whole surface covered in shredded nori
items.note: きざみ (kizami) = shredded; 一面 (ichimen) = the entire surface; まし (mashi) = extra. Plain seaweed, but it goes into a wheat-noodle bowl.

items.ja: クリスピーフライドオニオン
items.note: Fifty yen for a handful of crunch — the cheapest button on the machine and worth pressing. Fried onion is normally dusted in wheat flour.
チャーシュー (chāshū) is the braised/roasted pork loin that tops ramen; chopped small and heaped on rice with its own sauce. The machine's English reads 'Roasted pork rice bowl'.

A plain rice button sits in the small-button block; the price was not legible in the photograph of the machine, so check it on the day. Unseasoned steamed rice is safe on both counts — just don't let anyone ladle tare over it.
生 (nama) = 'raw', i.e. draught rather than bottled. Note the sign taped above the machine: the shop asks each customer to order one noodle dish and will not seat you for drinks alone.
There are also oolong tea (ウーロン茶) and Calpis (カルピス, a sweet milky soft drink) buttons on the same block.

kyr_ryouriya_terado.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Sushi and grill prices from the shop's own October 2025 menu posting; curry tsukemen prices from its own May 2025 posting. The shop now serves dinner only (17:00–22:00, closed Mondays), so the curry tsukemen that used to be a lunch dish is an evening order.

items.ja: ９貫握り寿司　味噌汁付き
items.en: Nine pieces of hand-pressed sushi, with miso soup
items.note: 貫 (kan) is the counter for a piece of nigiri — 九貫 is nine pieces, chef's selection. 味噌汁付き means miso soup is included (付き = 'comes with'). The shop prints its menu in Japanese, English, Chinese and Korean, so you can point. The sushi rice is fine; the soy sauce you dip in is wheat-brewed, and miso is often barley — bring your own tamari if that matters.

items.ja: ８貫握り寿司　味噌汁付き
items.en: Eight pieces of hand-pressed sushi, with miso soup
items.note: The same set one piece smaller — the standard order here.

雲丹 (uni) is sea urchin roe — creamy, briny, faintly sweet, and the single most expensive thing per bite in most sushi bars. Wrapped in a band of nori (軍艦, gunkan style) so it doesn't slide off. One piece, so you can try it without committing.
盛り合わせ (moriawase) = an assortment on one plate, chosen by the chef from what came in that day. Raw fish only, no rice. Soy sauce for dipping = wheat.

items.ja: 雲丹海鮮ちらし丼　味噌汁付き
items.en: Rice bowl scattered with sea urchin and mixed seafood, with miso soup
items.note: ちらし (chirashi) means 'scattered' — instead of individual nigiri, the fish is strewn over a bowl of seasoned sushi rice. 海鮮 (kaisen) = seafood generally. Easier to eat than nigiri if you are tired of chopstick precision.

items.ja: まぐろ５貫握りウニ乗せ
items.en: Five pieces of tuna nigiri, each crowned with sea urchin
items.note: 乗せ (nose) = 'placed on top'. The showpiece of the counter — lean red tuna with a spoonful of uni on each piece.
マグロ (maguro) is tuna — the default red-fleshed sushi fish. Five of the same, if you know what you like.
The safest order for a nervous first-timer, and the cheapest of the five-piece sets.

items.en: Half a wooden tray of Hokkaido sea urchin
items.note: Sold as 半箱, half of the flat wooden box (折 ori) that uni is graded and shipped in from Hokkaido — the tongues laid out in rows, eaten as they are. A splurge item, priced accordingly.

items.en: Salmon grilled in sweet Kyoto white miso
items.note: 西京 is an old name for Kyoto ('the western capital') and 西京味噌 is its pale, low-salt, very sweet rice-koji miso. The fish is buried in it for a day or two, then grilled — the miso caramelises and the flesh turns dense and sweet. One of the genuinely Kyoto things on this menu. Saikyo miso is normally rice-based rather than barley, but confirm, and the marinade usually contains mirin and sake.
Raw fish and prawn over leaves with a Japanese dressing — those are almost always soy- or dashi-based.
Prawn and vegetables in a light wheat-flour batter, with a lemon wedge. The dipping sauce, 天つゆ (tentsuyu), is dashi plus soy — so bonito and wheat both.

items.en: Noodles served dry, dipped into a curry broth
items.section: カレーつけ麺のメニュー
items.note: The dish that makes a Japanese restaurant show up under 'ramen' searches. つけ麺 (tsukemen) means the noodles arrive cold and naked on one plate and a small bowl of hot concentrated soup arrives beside them — you dip a few strands at a time rather than pouring it over. What makes this one Kyoto and not a ramen shop is the broth: the menu says お出汁の効いたカレースープ, a curry built on 出汁 (dashi, the kelp-and-bonito stock that underlies all Japanese cooking) rather than on stock cubes. Comes with chicken, half an egg, pickled radish and grilled vegetables. The shop also sells the soup frozen.

items.ja: 豚しゃぶカレーつけ麺
items.en: Curry tsukemen with cold poached pork
items.section: カレーつけ麺のメニュー
items.note: Marked 店主おすすめ — the owner's recommendation. しゃぶ from しゃぶしゃぶ: paper-thin pork swished through hot water for a few seconds and then chilled, so it stays soft. The menu calls the pork カレーと相性抜群, 'a superb match for the curry'.

items.ja: 魚の天ぷら付　カレーつけ麺
items.en: Curry tsukemen with a side of fish tempura
items.section: カレーつけ麺のメニュー
items.note: 付 (tsuki) = 'comes with'. The fish changes with the season — in summer it is often 鱧 (hamo, pike conger), the Kyoto summer fish whose fine bones have to be scored by hand before cooking. Described as サクッと軽い食感, light and crisp.

items.en: Curry tsukemen with beef and raw spring onion
items.section: カレーつけ麺のメニュー
items.note: 牛 (gyuu) beef with シャキシャキねぎ — shaki-shaki is the onomatopoeia for a crisp, squeaky-fresh crunch, so the onion is raw and heaped, not wilted. The most expensive of the four.

items.section: カレーつけ麺 トッピング
items.note: Order this with a curry tsukemen and tip it into the leftover dipping broth at the end — the standard tsukemen finish. Plain steamed rice with nothing on it is genuinely gluten-free and vegan.

items.section: カレーつけ麺 トッピング
items.note: 小 = small, 中 = medium. Same rice, bigger bowl.

items.section: カレーつけ麺 トッピング
items.note: 大盛 (oomori) = large; 玉 (tama) is the counter for a ball of noodles, so 1.5玉 is one and a half servings. Only ¥110 more.

kyr_menya_tsuki.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from a full-resolution photograph of the in-store menu, February 2026.

items.en: Brothless noodles in seasoned oil — the house speciality
items.note: Sizes step up cheaply: 並 200g ¥850, 大 300g ¥900, 特 400g ¥950, 特々 500g ¥1,000. There is no soup — a soy tare and an aromatic oil sit hidden under very thick noodles, and you must stir hard before the first bite. The shop's own note then tells you to reshape it with the vinegar (酢), chilli oil (ラー油) and onion on the table.

items.en: Plain abura-soba — noodles, tare, oil and nothing else
items.note: 並 ¥600 / 大 ¥650 / 特 ¥700 / 特々 ¥750. The menu says it comes with only shredded white leek and nori, and recommends it to people who want to build their own bowl from the topping list.
並 ¥900 / 大 ¥980. The shop's note: chicken bones and chicken meat simmered a long time for a broth of pure savour — 'simple, so the ingredients show'.

items.en: Ramen in Japanese dashi rather than meat broth
items.note: 並 ¥900 / 大 ¥980. Built on several kinds of dried-fish dashi plus kombu seaweed — the menu says outright that 'the dashi is the lead role'. Lighter and more Kyoto than a typical ramen.
Lactic-fermented bamboo, seasoned — usually in soy.
The near-universal ramen upgrade: jammy yolk, white stained brown by the soy tare.
Cooked just to setting so the yolk runs — on abura-soba it works as a sauce.
'White-hair leek' — sliced into threads and soaked so it curls and stays sharp.
Plain roasted nori; dunk it and wrap noodles in it.
Belly simmered in soy and sugar until it collapses.
The small, hard-worked muscle either side of the neck — springy and unusually rich. A yakitori cut, rare as a ramen topping.
The menu describes it as 'the golden ratio of tebasaki glaze and spice' — modelled on Nagoya's famous sweet-soy peppered chicken wings.

items.en: Okayama-style fried chicken in sweet-hot glaze
items.note: The menu calls the sweet-spicy sauce クセになる — habit-forming. Okayama's regional karaage is defined by being sauced rather than dry.

items.ja: 和風ヤンニョム唐揚げ
items.note: Korean sweet-chilli yangnyeom sauce crossed with Japanese red miso — the menu's own phrase is 和韓ミックス, a Japan-Korea mix.
2 pieces ¥300 / 4 pieces ¥500 / 6 pieces ¥650, with sauces at ¥90 each — spring-onion sauce, house tartare, chilli-oil relish or kimchi. Marinated in soy, dusted in starch and fried.
One of three ¥450 mini-bowls — the others are Okayama karaage and braised pork belly — meant as a partner to the noodles.
The same soy-braised belly used as a topping, over rice.

items.ja: クリームチーズのわさび漬け
items.en: Cream cheese cured in wasabi lees
items.note: A classic Japanese drinking snack — wasabi-zuke is wasabi stems pickled in sake lees; against cold cream cheese it goes sharp, then sweet.
Skin rendered until it shatters. Confirm the seasoning — usually salt, sometimes soy.

items.ja: うずらの特製醤油漬け
items.en: Quail eggs steeped in house soy
items.note: Small marinated eggs, one bite each — the same tare that seasons the noodles.

items.ja: 水餃子（塩ダレ・ラー油）
items.en: Boiled dumplings with salt tare and chilli oil
items.note: Poached rather than fried, dressed in a salt-based sauce instead of the usual soy-vinegar.
Small ¥150 / medium ¥200 / large ¥250. Order it with abura-soba and use it to mop up the tare left in the bowl — the same idea as 追い飯 (oimeshi). Raw egg over rice (TKG) is ¥300.

kyr_chugoku_ryori_saikaku.price_note: Prices are indicative only. The shop publishes no menu of its own; these come from diner write-ups of differing vintage (2017 onward) and have very likely risen. Treat them as a sense of scale, not a quote.

items.en: Soupless dan dan noodles — the dish people come for
items.note: A Bib Gourmand kitchen's version: sesame paste cut with Chinese black vinegar, a heap of minced pork miso and finely chopped white leek over low-hydration thin noodles that stay crumbly-firm. There is no broth — stir it thoroughly before the first bite. Diners note the black-vinegar-and-sesame pairing makes it read oddly like a spicy sauce-yakisoba.
The soup version of the same idea. Lunch runs Wednesday to Friday only and the kitchen is a one-man operation, so food and the bill can both be slow — that is the trade for the cooking.
Regulars describe the house style as 濃くない四川 — Sichuan without the heaviness: the numbing sansho aroma is all there, but the dish is not drowned in oil.

items.en: Sichuan-style simmered beef in chilli oil
items.note: Arrives still boiling. Under a drift of whole dried chillies — seasoning, not food, so do not try to eat them — sit soft starch-coated beef, mushrooms and pak choi beneath a two-centimetre float of chilli oil. The house's most aggressive dish.
Ebi-chili — a Sichuan dish rebuilt for Japanese palates in the 1950s, tomato-sweetened as much as hot.
Pork belly simmered, sliced, then returned to a hot wok with cabbage and sweet bean paste. Diners call it the strongest possible partner for plain rice.

items.en: Sweet and sour pork with black vinegar
items.note: Chinese black vinegar is aged and malty rather than sharp, so the sauce comes out dark and mellow instead of neon.

items.ja: 鶏肉の山椒唐辛子炒め
items.en: Chicken stir-fried with sansho pepper and chilli
items.note: The Sichuan 麻辣 (mala) pairing — sansho for the numbing tingle, chilli for the burn.

items.en: 'Mouth-watering chicken' — cold poached chicken in chilli oil
items.note: The name is literal: a Sichuan classic of sliced poached chicken under garlic, sansho, sesame and chilli oil, said to make you drool at the mere thought of it.
XO sauce is a Hong Kong invention of dried scallop, dried shrimp, ham and chilli — expensive, intensely savoury, and named after XO cognac purely for prestige.

items.en: Tofu simmered with leek in a mild thick sauce
items.note: The least spicy thing on the menu and, by several accounts, one of the best: a whole block of tofu with shiitake and wood-ear fungus under a gentle sweet starch-thickened sauce. Best in cold weather.

items.en: Assortment of three appetisers, chef's choice
items.note: Priced for two. One reported set: ginger-scented steamed chicken, small prawns fried and finished tsukudani-style, and edamame steeped in green-sansho soy — all built as things to drink over. The shop keeps thirty-plus bottles including baijiu, sherry and aged Shaoxing.

items.ja: きゅうりとイカの山椒オイルあえ
items.romaji: Kyuuri to Ika no Sanshou Oiru Ae
items.en: Cucumber and squid dressed in sansho oil
items.note: Named by a recent diner as the dish locals insist you order. Cold, crunchy and numbing from the pepper oil.

items.ja: まこも茸といんげん、ひき肉と芽菜の煎り炒め
items.romaji: Makomodake to Ingen, Hikiniku to Yasai no Iri-itame
items.en: Wild-rice stem and green beans stir-fried with minced pork and preserved mustard
items.note: An original the shop is known for and that diners say they have never met elsewhere. 真菰筍 (makomodake) is the swollen stem of wild rice grass, crisp like a water chestnut; dried shrimp hides in the mince.

kyr_chugoku_ryori_kuretake.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The shop publishes dish names but not a full price list; the few prices below come from dated diner reports. Budget is roughly ¥1,000-2,000 a head at either meal.

items.section: 前菜・揚げ物 / Starters & fried
items.note: The plate almost every table orders. Wheat wrappers, soy-vinegar dip.

items.section: 前菜・揚げ物 / Starters & fried
items.note: Pleated cylinders of minced pork in a thin wheat wrapper, steamed rather than fried.

items.section: 前菜・揚げ物 / Starters & fried
items.note: Wheat pastry around pork and shredded vegetables, deep fried.

items.ja: 鶏の唐揚げ香味ソース
items.section: 前菜・揚げ物 / Starters & fried
items.note: 香味 (koumi) means the sauce is built on spring onion, ginger and garlic — a sharper, more Chinese treatment than plain karaage.
Tofu and minced pork in fermented broad-bean chilli paste, numbing with sansho pepper. The 四川 prefix signals they make it properly hot rather than the mild Japanese version.
Battered pork with peppers and onion in a glossy vinegar-sugar sauce. Battered and soy-seasoned — wheat twice over.

items.ja: ピーマンと豚肉の細切炒め
items.romaji: Piiman to Butaniku no Hosogiri Itame
items.en: Shredded pork and green pepper stir-fry
items.note: The Japanese-Chinese take on 青椒肉絲 (chinjao rosu) — everything cut to matchsticks so it cooks in seconds.

items.ja: キャベツと豚肉の味噌炒め
items.romaji: Kyabetsu to Butaniku no Miso Itame
items.en: Pork and cabbage stir-fried in miso
items.note: The Japanese reading of 回鍋肉 (hoikoro), twice-cooked pork. Miso here may be barley-based as well as soy.
Price seen as a 定食 set. Pork, squid, prawn, quail eggs and vegetables bound in a light starch-thickened sauce — the mildest thing on a machi-chuka menu and the standard order for children.
Served flat under a thickened sweet-sour sauce; poured over rice it becomes 天津飯.
The chilli-sauce treatment usually reserved for prawns, applied to aubergine — soft, sweet and hot. The sauce base normally contains stock and soy, so confirm before assuming it is meat-free.
Belly simmered until the fat turns translucent, in soy, sugar and spice.

items.en: Nagasaki champon — noodles in milky pork broth
items.note: A Nagasaki dish of Chinese-immigrant origin: thick noodles boiled directly in a cloudy pork-and-chicken broth loaded with cabbage, pork, squid, prawn and fish cake. Heartier and less refined than ramen, deliberately so.
Champon's dry sibling, also from Nagasaki, containing no udon at all: fine noodles fried crisp then buried under a thick seafood-and-vegetable sauce.
Sesame-and-chilli broth with minced pork. A chilled version (冷やし担々麺) appears in summer.

On from late November to early March. 酒粕 is the pressed lees left after brewing sake, and Fushimi is one of Japan's great sake districts — so this is a genuinely local bowl: thick, cloudy and faintly boozy-sweet. A 酒粕担々麺 runs alongside it.

items.ja: 五目あんかけやきそば
items.en: Fried noodles under a mixed gravy
items.note: Noodles crisped in the pan, then a starch-thickened stir-fry poured over so the top goes soft while the base stays crunchy.
The Kansai word for chahan. Egg, spring onion and pork, seasoned with soy.

One reported version: prawns and vegetables stir-fried in a light salt sauce, boiled dumplings, pickled mustard greens, egg soup, rice, jasmine tea and almond jelly. Contents rotate, and there is a 日替わりランチ (daily lunch) on weekdays.
Apricot-kernel milk jelly — the standard close to a Chinese meal in Japan. Contains dairy.

kyr_dashi_ryori_jifu.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The shop's own site sells dashi kits rather than listing the dine-in menu; the dishes below were documented by visiting writers, and the day's offer is short and shifts.

items.en: Ultra-thin house noodles in clear dashi, seasoned only with salt
items.note: Also written oだしのニューめん. The whole shop in one bowl: broth from Rishiri kombu, sawara (Spanish mackerel) bushi and katsuobushi, seasoned with nothing but about one gram of rock salt from Noda in Iwate — no soy sauce at all, which is why the dashi reads so clearly. The noodles are made in-house from domestic wheat and egg only. Topped with bonito shaved to order and salt-pickled green sansho peppercorns.

items.en: Breakfast set built around dashi drawn to order
items.note: 引きたて (hikitate) means the dashi is pulled fresh in front of you. Served with tuna-bushi flakes, olive oil and salt; the second serving comes with mountain-wasabi soy sauce — that part is wheat, so decline it if you need to.

items.ja: まぐろ節のたまごかけごはん
items.en: Raw egg over rice with dried tuna flakes
items.note: TKG — the Japanese breakfast of raw egg stirred into hot rice — here made with eggs from hens fed Uji tea leaves, and dressed with salt and olive oil instead of the usual soy sauce.

items.en: Drinking dashi, served in a cup
items.note: Dashi to drink like coffee, available to take away. Kombu and dried fish with salt and nothing else. The owner opened the shop to teach people what dashi actually tastes like, partly out of alarm that Hokkaido kombu harvests have halved in fifty years.
Finished with salt rather than the usual soy, consistent with the kitchen's no-soy-sauce habit — worth confirming on the day.

items.ja: まぐろ節の和風パスタ
items.en: Japanese-style pasta with dried tuna flakes
items.note: Wheat pasta dressed in the house dashi idiom rather than a Western sauce.

Sold at the counter alongside the food — kombu and fish flakes portioned for one pot, with the owner's method: cold water with kombu and small dried fish, bring to a boil, simmer gently three minutes, then add the bonito.

items.note: 8 slices ¥1,800 / 4 slices ¥1,000. The reason this shop exists: a loin of skipjack scorched over blazing rice straw so the outside chars and smokes while the centre stays raw, then sliced thick. 土佐 (Tosa) is the old name for Kochi, where the dish comes from — eaten there with heaps of sliced garlic and either salt or ponzu. Ponzu contains soy sauce; ask for salt if you need to avoid wheat.

Only a few grams per bird, so it is the cut regulars order first — springy, fatty, deeply chickeny. Every yakitori here is ¥400. You will be asked 塩かタレか, salt or the sweet soy glaze; the glaze is wheat soy.
The default, forgiving cut — juicy dark meat. Often called かしわ (kashiwa) in western Japan.
Chicken minced with cartilage and aromatics for texture, packed onto the skewer. Usually bound with a little flour or breadcrumb as well as glazed in soy.
Grilled long and slow until the fat renders out and the edges go to glass. Ask for it カリカリ (karikari) — well crisped.
The grinding stomach muscle — crunchy rather than chewy, almost no fat, usually served with salt.
From the English 'hearts'. Dense, clean, slightly mineral — a good first offal skewer.
Also written レバー (rebaa). Cooked to just-pink it goes custardy; almost always finished in the sweet soy tare.
The nub of fatty meat above the tail — one per bird, and the richest thing on the grill.
Wing tip and mid-joint; eaten with fingers, worked off the two bones.
Marked おすすめ (recommended). Not chicken, but standard on any Japanese grill.

A 京野菜 — one of Kyoto's protected heirloom vegetables, bred in Maizuru around 1920. Long, thin-walled and almost entirely mild, with the very occasional hot one. Grilled whole until it blisters. Salt seasoning is fine; soy is not, so ask.
Caps grilled gill-side up so the juices pool. Ask whether it is finished with salt or soy.
Cut into blocks and charred until the middle turns to sweet slush.
Pressed tofu scored and grilled; the standard glaze is soy-based, so confirm.

items.en: Grilled broad beans in the pod
items.note: Charred whole in the pod and salted; you split them open at the table.

Egg beaten with a great deal of dashi and rolled in thin layers in a rectangular pan — the Kyoto version is savoury and wet rather than sweet. Usually seasoned with a little light soy (usukuchi), which is still wheat.
A cold block of tofu with ginger, spring onion and bonito flakes — the flakes and the poured soy are what disqualify it; ask for it plain and it is neither.
Smashed cucumber in sesame oil, garlic and chilli — the standard palate-reset between skewers.
Hirai beef is a Kochi-raised wagyu, tying the croquette to the shop's Tosa theme; the steak itself is on the menu at ¥3,850. Panko-crumbed and deep-fried — wheat throughout.
Split flat, salted and grilled — a big, oily, flaky northern fish that is a fixture of Japanese drinking menus. Salt only, no soy.
